ledger.claim: The distances on the platform's own trip record establish the deviation: actual 9.5 km against a recommended 8.1 km is 1.40 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the threshold limb of POL-RD-22 is met. The same record's event log fixes the route taken and when — route_deviation_detected at 08:42:55 leaving the PIE at Clementi Avenue 6, route_rejoined at 08:53:16 at Holland Road / Commonwealth Avenue West. The driver-device trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (37 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap above 120 s) and independently places the vehicle on Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West across that same ten-minute window, so neither the fact of the deviation nor its window is in dispute.

POL-RD-21 requires the driver to tell the rider of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. Neither happened here. The chat log carries two messages only, sent at 08:35:52 and 08:36:12 — both before the trip started at 08:37:22, both about the pickup point ('I'm at Westgate taxi stand, white Corolla' and 'Ok') — and the record's messages_during_trip array is empty and in_app_calls is empty. The rider's 'Ok' therefore cannot be an acknowledgment of a deviation: it answers a pickup message six minutes before the deviation occurred, and the driver's own statement on file concedes the omission in terms ('Forgot to inform, sorry'). No notice also means no agreement, which is what row (a) of the refund matrix would require.

Exactly one row of POL-RD-24 applies, and on this record both candidate rows end in the same refund, so the refund does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved. If the reroute was traffic-justified, the case is row (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare. If it was not traffic-justified, the case is row (d): not justified, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare in full. There is no row on this record on which the rider keeps carrying the excess distance fare, and row (a) is closed off because agreement is not established on the chat log or any recording.

The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD, which is the figure the fare ledger's own derivation records. The ledger shows the rider was charged 14.78 SGD in total with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so none of the 1.01 SGD has been returned and the present state still has the rider carrying it. The claim text asks for 4.00 SGD; the policy's own arithmetic caps the recovery at the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD, and that is the amount the matrix provides — the point is that it moves to the rider, not that the rider should keep paying it.

The traffic advisory does not close the justification question, and it does not have to be resolved in the driver's favour. Its own derived facts record intersects_route as null, with the note that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route' — so whether it justifies the reroute is a question the Judge decides from its road, direction and location under POL-RD-23, not a fact the advisory settles. Even taken at its highest for the driver, POL-RD-23 only converts the case into row (b) of POL-RD-24, which refunds the same excess distance fare; and the driver's bare assertion that the PIE was jammed cannot itself supply the missing connection.

No fact this case needs is missing or impaired, so POL-GEN-26 does not send this to a human. The deviation distance is established on the trip record and corroborated by a COMPLETE GPS trace, the notification question is settled by a COMPLETE chat log read against a COMPLETE call list, the redundancy of the two refund rows makes the advisory's undetermined intersection immaterial to the outcome, and the fare arithmetic is drawn from a COMPLETE payments ledger. Nothing in POL-GEN-26's list of open questions is actually open here, and there is therefore no basis to escalate rather than refund.

The AI can and should issue this ruling finally rather than pass it up. The dispute value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band, and no fraud flag is carried by either party, so no elevated confidence applies. POL-RD-25 sets 0.80 for a route deviation; every artifact that carries a deciding fact here — trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger, advisory — is graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes, so POL-GEN-02's impairment cap bites on nothing and the 0.80 threshold is clearly available on this record. The outcome should be a refund, not a held amount.

Neither party's profile can decide this trip, and the only profile fields that could ever raise the bar for an AI ruling — the fraud flags — are absent on both sides, so nothing in the profile history is a reason to deny this claim. Under POL-GEN-01 these snapshots may inform how closely assertions are scrutinised and nothing more; the deciding facts here are the device trace, the route events and the fare ledger, not either party's record.

Under POL-RD-24 the only money the matrix can move on a route deviation is the excess distance fare, and the policy's own arithmetic on this fare breakdown gives 1.01 SGD: deviation 1.40 km x per-km rate 0.72 SGD, no surge, rounded to the cent. That figure is carried in the fare breakdown's derived money block as excess_distance_fare_sgd. The rider's claim for 4.00 SGD is unsupported by the fare record; the driver's maximum exposure on this trip is 1.01 SGD, not 4.00 SGD.

The deviation distance is fixed at 1.40 km by the platform's recorded distances under POL-RD-22: 9.5 km actual less 8.1 km recommended. POL-RD-22 expressly bars re-measuring the deviation from the GPS trace, because a sparse trace understates a route's length, so neither side may substitute the trace distance. On the recorded distances the deviation exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, and the driver does not claim the within-tolerance rows; the consequence is confined to the excess distance fare the first claim identifies.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory, which is an admissible congestion type in POL-RD-23's type table; it is on the Pan-Island Expressway, which the recorded recommended route uses; and it is valid 08:15:42 to 09:27:22, overlapping the trip window (started 08:37:22, ended 08:55:22). Its stated location, 'after Clementi Avenue 6 exit to Clementi Road exit', is the very stretch the trip record names when it logs the vehicle leaving the recommended route at 08:42:55 at 'PIE / Clementi Avenue 6 exit'. The driver left the recommended route at the point the congestion advisory begins, on a permitted reroute in response to real traffic, not a detour of his own choosing. The pre-pass leaves the route-intersection question to the Judge rather than deciding it, and the driver asks the Judge to decide it on the advisory's own road, direction and location fields read against the recorded route.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation, and the driver does not press the no-refund row. The chat log holds two messages only, both sent before pickup and both about the meeting point, with no deviation notice, and the driver's own statement says he forgot to inform. POL-RD-21's notification obligation is therefore not met and row (a) of POL-RD-24 is unavailable. But the failure to notify does not enlarge the remedy: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both award the excess distance fare and nothing more, so non-notification caps out at the same 1.01 SGD already fixed by the policy formula.

No part of the contested toll is attributable to the deviation: the single ERP charge of 1.00 SGD was incurred at the PIE gantry at 08:40:36, more than two minutes before the vehicle left the recommended route at 08:42:55, so the toll was incurred on the recommended stretch and is not part of the excess distance the deviation produced. This forecloses any attempt to fold the toll into the refund on top of the excess distance fare.

This case is decided on the record and is not an escalation. The contested amount is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and no fraud_flags entry appears on either party's profile snapshot, so the 0.95 uplift does not apply; POL-RD-25 adds nothing here because POL-GEN-22 permits the ruling. Every fact POL-RD-24 needs on this case - the deviation distance, the notification position, the traffic data for the recommended route - is carried by complete, weight-1.0 artifacts, so POL-GEN-26 has no open question to escalate.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: after testing both sides' claims against the record, part of the trip charge is returned — 1.01 SGD — and the rest of the charge stands.

How far the vehicle went. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation from the platform's own recorded distances: actual 9.5 km less recommended 8.1 km = 1.40 km (EV-TRIP-05004). That is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the deviation is real and material. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05004) shows which roads were used — Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West across the 08:42:55 to 08:53:16 window — but POL-RD-22 says the trace is not used to re-measure distance, so the 1.40 km figure from the trip record governs. Both sides' claims on this point are accepted.

Whether the rider was told. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat (or a recorded verbal notice) before or at the deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05004) carries only two messages, both sent before the trip started and both about the meeting point; the record shows no messages and no calls during the trip, and the driver's own statement on file concedes he forgot to inform. The rider's single 'Ok' was an answer to a pickup message six minutes before the deviation and is not acknowledgment of it. Both sides' claims are accepted on this point.

Whether traffic justified the reroute. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05004-01) is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC type, which POL-RD-23 counts as admissible congestion. It is on the Pan-Island Expressway, the road the recommended route uses; its stated stretch (PIE towards Changi, after Clementi Avenue 6 exit to Clementi Road exit) is the recommended route's own segment, travelled in the direction of this trip; and it is valid 08:15:42 to 09:27:22, overlapping the trip window. The driver left the recommended route at 08:42:55 exactly at the Clementi Avenue 6 exit where that congestion begins. On the advisory's own road, direction and location read against the recorded route, the reroute was a response to real congestion and is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23.

The refund. POL-RD-24's matrix applies. The applicable row is (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare. This is why the driver's reliance on the justification does not avoid a refund, and the rider's request is scaled to what the policy provides. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD (EV-FARE-05004). The rider's claim text asks for 4.00 SGD; the fare record does not support that figure, and POL-RD-24 caps the recovery at 1.01 SGD. The single ERP charge of 1.00 SGD was incurred at 08:40:36, more than two minutes before the vehicle left the recommended route, so it was incurred on the recommended stretch and is not part of the excess — the driver's claim on this is accepted.

The outcome is the same whether the traffic question is answered for the driver (row (b)) or against him (row (d)): both award the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD. Nothing this case needs is missing or impaired, so POL-GEN-26 does not send it to a human reviewer: the deviation distance comes from a COMPLETE trip record, the notification position from a COMPLETE chat log and call list, the traffic data from a COMPLETE advisory, and the fare from a COMPLETE payments ledger. The contested amount is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither party carries a fraud flag (POL-GEN-01, POL-GEN-22); and the confidence here is 0.9, above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for a route deviation. No referral clause fires on this case.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
